brief: A great README is a hiring tool — 6 patterns OSS maintainers swear by.

slots.subText: OSS maintainers use six proven patterns to turn skim-readers into committed contributors.

slots.title: Start with a crystal
slots.subtitle: Explain what it does in one line before anyone scrolls.
slots.b1Body: Visitors bounce if the headline doesn't speak their language instantly.
slots.b2Body: Replace buzzwords with the exact pain point your tool removes.

slots.title: Ship a copy-paste
slots.subtitle: Get users to "hello world" in under sixty seconds flat.
slots.b1Body: The fastest path to value beats a thousand feature paragraphs.
slots.b2Body: A terminal screenshot proves your project works without configuration hell.

slots.title: Frame the problem
slots.subtitle: Readers buy the "why" before they care about the "how".
slots.b1Body: Show the ugly status quo, then reveal your elegant escape hatch.
slots.b2Body: Concrete examples beat abstract claims when recruiting technical talent.

slots.title: Document the hidden
slots.subtitle: Explain trade-offs so senior engineers can debate and buy in.
slots.b1Body: A simple diagram turns strangers into architects who trust your judgment.
slots.b2Body: Honest limits attract collaborators more than polished marketing ever could.

slots.title: Lower the contribution
slots.subtitle: Good-first-issue labels and setup scripts turn lurkers into committers.
slots.b1Body: Explicit starter tasks signal a community that mentors rather than gatekeeps.
slots.b2Body: One script to configure dev envs removes friction that kills enthusiasm.

slots.title: Show social proof
slots.subtitle: Stars and adopters signal that talented engineers already trust this.
slots.b1Body: Company logos and testimonials imply production-grade reliability and career growth.
slots.b2Body: A public changelog proves the project is alive and professionally maintained.

slots.ctaBody: Apply these six patterns and watch your repository become a magnet for talent instead of a graveyard of confusion.
